questions.stem: A DevOps engineer uses AWS CloudFormation to create a connection to GitHub and an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses it as the source. The stack deploys successfully, but the pipeline cannot access the repository, and the connection status is PENDING. The engineer wants to keep the connection that the stack created and avoid storing personal tokens. What should the engineer do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Wait for the connection to change to AVAILABLE automatically after the first pipeline run.
Delete the connection and create it again with the AWS CLI so that it becomes AVAILABLE.
Edit the connection in the console to complete its setup so that its status becomes AVAILABLE.
Store a GitHub personal access token in AWS Secrets Manager and point the source action to it.

questions.stem: An AWS CodePipeline pipeline uses a GitHub source action through a connection, followed by an AWS CodeBuild action. The build script runs git commands that read the commit history to compute a version number, but the commands fail because no Git metadata is present. A later AWS CodeDeploy action must keep receiving the build output. The team does not want to store Git credentials in the build. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Configure the source action to output a full clone, and keep CodeBuild as the action that uses the source artifact.
Configure the source action to output a full clone, and pass the source artifact directly to the CodeDeploy action.
Keep the default ZIP output and add a git clone command that uses a personal access token to the buildspec.
Keep the default ZIP output and run git init in the build before the version script runs.

questions.stem: A company's AWS CodePipeline pipeline uses a GitHub source through a connection and currently starts on every push. The company wants the pipeline to start only when a Git tag whose name starts with "release" is created. Pushes without such a tag must not start the pipeline, and the company does not want to write custom code. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Configure the pipeline trigger with the Tags filter type and the pattern release*.
Keep the push trigger and add a branch filter for the main branch, where release tags are created.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for GitHub tag events that invokes a Lambda function to start the pipeline.
Disable automatic starts and choose Release change in the console after each release tag is created.
